title.en: The Cartesian plane, coordinates and distances

text.en: Reiaan sketches his new room on graph paper to place his bed, desk and door. To tell a friend exactly where each thing is, he needs just two numbers for every position. That is the idea of coordinates.

To locate a point in a plane we use two perpendicular lines: a horizontal x-axis and a vertical y-axis, meeting at the origin O with coordinates (0, 0).
The distance of a point from the y-axis is its x-coordinate, and the distance from the x-axis is its y-coordinate, written as the ordered pair (x, y).
A point on the x-axis has the form (x, 0), and a point on the y-axis has the form (0, y).
The axes divide the plane into four quadrants. The signs are (+, +) in Quadrant I, (-, +) in II, (-, -) in III and (+, -) in IV.
The order matters: (x, y) equals (y, x) only when x = y.
For points on the same horizontal line, the distance is the absolute value of the difference of the x-coordinates, for example from (3, 4) to (7, 4) it is 4.
For any two points we make a right triangle and use the Baudhayana-Pythagoras theorem. From A (3, 4) to D (7, 1) the legs are 4 and 3, so AD = 5.
Reflecting a point in the y-axis changes the sign of its x-coordinate, so M (9, 6) goes to M' (-9, 6).

problem.en: Find the distance between P (2, 3) and Q (6, 6).

why.en: Make a right triangle with these legs.

prompt.en: How do coordinates fix a point and how do you find the distance between two points?

requiredIdeas.en: Two perpendicular axes and an origin
x is distance from y-axis, y from x-axis
Right triangle and the theorem for distance

points.en: The coordinate plane has an x-axis, a y-axis and the origin (0, 0).
A point is written (x, y); points on the axes are (x, 0) and (0, y).
Quadrant signs: I (+,+), II (-,+), III (-,-), IV (+,-).
Distances come from differences of coordinates and the theorem.
